issues.item: Triggers: Sexual Trauma Cues: Comments on sexual violence
issues.explanation: For a mugging/robbery trauma, comments on sexual violence are a hard-to-explain trigger unless the robbery also involved a sexual assault component, which is not indicated. This trigger does not fit the validated trauma type and is not supported by the rest of the profile.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: No Accountability: The people responsible have faced no consequences
issues.explanation: The appraisal that nothing has been done about it / no consequences is not impossible after a robbery, but paired with 'Authority Presence: Police' as a trigger it creates tension: police-related cues imply salient contact with authorities, whereas these appraisals imply a justice-focused grievance. This could occur, but here the profile lacks supporting memory or threat content about failed reporting or ongoing legal injustice, making the appraisal cluster feel mismatched to the rest of the formulation.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Injustice: What happened to me was deeply unfair and nothing has been done about it
issues.explanation: Similarly, 'deeply unfair and nothing has been done about it' is overly justice-system focused relative to the rest of the profile. With robbery trauma and the given items, the profile is otherwise centered on hypervigilance and sensory re-experiencing; this item would be more coherent if there were corroborating content about reporting, police failure, or perpetrator impunity.

issues.item: Triggers: Sexual Trauma Cues: Comments on sexual violence
issues.explanation: For a mugging or robbery trauma, 'comments on sexual violence' is a hard-to-explain trigger unless there is additional unreported sexual trauma content. It does not fit the stated trauma type, and the rest of the profile does not provide any bridge to sexual trauma themes.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Lost Emotions: I will never be able to feel normal emotions again
issues.explanation: 'I will never be able to feel normal emotions again' is possible in PTSD, but here it sits awkwardly with the rest of the selected appraisals, which are tightly focused on injustice and lack of consequences for perpetrators. This item shifts to a pervasive emotional numbing/irreversible damage theme that is not otherwise represented in the trigger, memory, or threat items, making the appraisal set less coherent.

issues.item: Triggers: Sexual Trauma Cues: Comments on sexual violence
issues.explanation: For a mugging or robbery trauma, police presence and feeling watched are plausible triggers, but comments on sexual violence are hard to reconcile unless there was an additional sexual-trauma component, which is not indicated by the trauma type. This item is therefore clinically implausible for the stated trauma.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Lost Emotions: I will never be able to feel normal emotions again
issues.explanation: The appraisal 'I will never be able to feel normal emotions again' reflects a broad enduring emotional numbing/irreversible change theme, but the rest of the profile is dominated by external danger, injustice, vigilance, and sensory trauma-memory content linked to mugging-related threat. It is not impossible, but in this profile it stands out as insufficiently supported by the other selected items and weakly aligned with the formulation pattern.

issues.item: Sexual Trauma Cues: Comments on sexual violence
issues.explanation: The trigger 'Comments on sexual violence' is hard to reconcile with the validated trauma type of mugging or robbery in the absence of any sexual-assault-related content elsewhere in the profile. This is not just unusual; it suggests a different trauma context than the rest of the self-report.

issues.item: No Accountability: The people responsible have faced no consequences
issues.explanation: The appraisal 'The people responsible have faced no consequences' is not impossible after a robbery, but paired with 'nothing has been done about it' it implies a justice/failure-to-prosecute theme. That can fit a robbery, yet it sits awkwardly with the rest of the profile because no other items reference police response, legal aftermath, or perpetrator accountability beyond police as a trigger.
